name: Vectorpea
tagline: Browser-based vector graphics editor from the Photopea camp, Illustrator-shaped, no install.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: An agent can absolutely give you a browser SVG editor in one session: rectangles, ellipses, a pen tool, node dragging, fill and stroke, layers, undo, export. That covers maybe the first hour of what you actually do in a vector editor. The part that takes person-years is everything after: boolean path operations, stroke-to-path and offsetting, snapping and alignment that feels right, a real text engine with font loading and kerning, gradients and clipping and filters, and importing AI, PDF, EPS and SVG files that were written by software that hates you. None of that is network effects or proprietary data, which is why this feels one-shottable, and it is still not. Build the toy if you only ever nudge SVG nodes; keep the tab open for anything real.
coreLoopDIY: A local single-page SVG editor with shape and pen tools, node editing, layers, undo, and SVG/PNG export.
requirements: some comfort with bezier math and pointer event handling
willingness to hand-roll geometry instead of importing a design app
whatYouLose: Import of AI, PDF, EPS, CDR and messy real-world SVG files
Boolean path ops, offset paths, stroke-to-path, shape builder
A real text engine: font loading, kerning, text on path, wrapping
Gradients, patterns, clipping, masks, blend modes and effects
Interaction polish: snapping, smart guides, alignment, keyboard muscle memory that matches Illustrator
moatNotes: The proprietary part is not a model in the AI sense, it is a hand-written geometry and file-parsing engine that has no open equivalent of comparable quality.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the alternative is either a desktop subscription or a two hour wrestle with an editor that cannot open the file a client sent. Browser vector editors win on zero install and on reading formats nobody wants to implement twice, and the paid tier is mostly buying quiet and removed ads rather than features. The price is low enough that the DIY math only works if you enjoy writing bezier code for its own sake.
notes: The shape tools are a weekend; the file importers and the geometry engine are not. The moat is person-years of bezier math, format parsing, and interaction polish crammed into one browser tab.
prompt:
Build a local, offline, single-page vector editor called "Peapod" in an empty folder.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Vite + TypeScript, no UI framework.
- Render the document as live SVG DOM in the page (not canvas). The SVG IS the document model.
- Zero backend, zero accounts, zero telemetry, zero network calls. No .env needed because there are no secrets.

In scope:
- Infinite canvas with pan (space drag, middle drag) and zoom (ctrl+wheel), plus a fixed-size artboard rect.
- Tools: select/move, rectangle, ellipse, line, pen (click for corner nodes, drag for bezier handles, enter/escape to finish), and direct-select for editing existing path nodes and handles.
- Selection: click, shift-click for multi, marquee drag. Bounding box with 8 resize handles and a rotate handle.
- Inspector panel: fill color, stroke color, stroke width, opacity, and x/y/w/h numeric fields.
- Layers panel: flat list, reorder by drag, rename, toggle visibility, lock, delete.
- Undo/redo: full snapshot-based history stack, ctrl+z / ctrl+shift+z, cap at 100 steps.
- Persistence: autosave the document to localStorage on every commit, restore on load.
- Export: download .svg (serialize the artboard subtree, cleaned) and .png (rasterize via an offscreen canvas at 1x/2x).
- Import: plain .svg files only, appended as a group. Warn loudly and clearly on anything it cannot parse.
- Keyboard: v/r/e/l/p tool shortcuts, delete, ctrl+d duplicate, arrow nudge, shift+arrow big nudge.

Explicitly out of scope, do not attempt, do not stub with fake buttons:
- Boolean path operations, offset path, stroke-to-path.
- Text of any kind, gradients, patterns, masks, clipping, filters, blend modes.
- AI, PDF, EPS, CDR import. Groups beyond a single flat level. Collaboration.

Quality bar:
- Pointer math must be correct under zoom and pan; write a single screenToDoc helper and use it everywhere.
- Keep geometry in its own module with unit tests for bezier point/handle math.
- README with run instructions and a blunt list of what this cannot do.
